description: Executable evidence for the personal blocklist obligations: whole-value CAS on one shared revision counter, the closed target set, receive-before-filter on shared history, projection rebuild after unblocking, and the non-enumerability of the filtered outcome.

decision_points.requirement: The blocklist is a whole-value CAS result whose version is exactly current + 1, and ak.account_data.set on the same key shares that one counter.
v1 registers no organization or realm blocklist target; official accounts and services are filtered by their exact ActorId.
Shared history is received and retained first and filtered holder-side afterwards; the sender observes nothing.
The next revision stops the filtering immediately and the holder view is rebuilt from already retained material.
No surface lets the sender, the queried party or a federation peer distinguish blocked from unauthorized, absent or offline, including from a device whose blocklist freshness is unknown.

cases.name: whole_value_cas_rejects_a_skipped_revision
cases.given: the holder's accepted ak.account.blocklist current result is at version 7
cases.action: author a whole-value blocklist write declaring version 9
cases.observed: the authority-committed typed current result and the rejected submission outcome
assertions: version MUST be exactly current + 1; 9 skips 8 and is refused
the accepted current result still reads version 7 after the refusal
no partial entry set is written

cases.name: whole_value_cas_rejects_a_stale_concurrent_write
cases.given: two holder devices both read version 7 and both author version 8
cases.action: commit the first write, then submit the second
cases.observed: both submission outcomes against one accepted stream
assertions: exactly one version 8 is accepted
the loser is refused rather than merged entry by entry: the blocklist is a whole-value result
the loser MUST re-read version 8 and re-author instead of retrying the same body

cases.name: account_data_set_shares_the_one_revision_counter
cases.given: ak.account.blocklist is at version 7 for this exact AccountId
cases.action: write ak.account_data.set on key ak.account.blocklist declaring version 8 after a concurrent blocklist write already took 8
cases.observed: the single revision counter shared by both authoring surfaces
assertions: the two surfaces MUST NOT form two independent winner chains
the counter is per exact AccountId: an account sharing a principal core on another Station shares neither counter nor rules

cases.name: target_closure_rejects_realm_and_organization_targets
cases.given: v1 defines no organization or realm blocklist target
cases.action: author a blocklist entry whose target names a Realm, then one naming an Organization
cases.observed: the payload validation outcome for each target form
assertions: an Organization's official account is filtered by its exact account ActorId and a service by its service ActorId
whole-Realm notification or default-view preferences are a separate per-Realm client preference and MUST NOT be synthesized out of a personal blocklist
leaving, refusing new writes or revoking sharing use the membership, Contact and capability paths instead

cases.name: shared_history_is_received_then_filtered_by_the_holder
cases.given: a blocked peer authors an Event in a Realm both accounts belong to
cases.action: sync the Realm stream on a holder device that already holds the blocking revision
cases.observed: the accepted Realm stream and the holder-side projection built from it
assertions: the Event is received and retained: a personal blocklist does not change the Realm's shared facts
the holder projection filters it after receipt
the peer's submission succeeds and receives no blocked_by_user signal, no distinguishable error, no latency difference and no delivery receipt difference

cases.name: unblock_rebuilds_the_projection_from_retained_material
cases.given: the holder blocked a peer and then authored the next revision removing that entry
cases.action: recompute the holder projection from the material already retained
cases.observed: the projection before and after the removing revision
assertions: future projections stop filtering immediately at the new revision
shared Realm and DM history received normally during the block reappears in the holder view
requests actually refused by a Contact tombstone during the block are not back-filled by unblocking
hiding old content after an unblock requires a holder-private hide or tombstone, or the erasure flow, and never a re-reading of blocklist removal as history deletion

cases.name: server_side_filtering_stays_indistinguishable
cases.given: the holder has explicitly authorized a service to read the blocklist data class
cases.action: a blocked sender submits a contact request, a first DM invite and a call invite
cases.observed: the sender-visible response shape, reason code and timing on each surface
assertions: the filtered outcome MUST NOT let the sender, the queried party or a federation peer separate blocked from unauthorized, absent or offline
a service without that explicit authorization forwards the encrypted material unchanged for client-side filtering instead of dropping it
no blocked_by_user reason reaches the sender on either path

cases.name: an_unsynced_device_treats_freshness_as_unknown
cases.given: one holder device has not yet synced the newest accepted blocklist revision
cases.action: ask that device to render the holder projection and to emit presence and read receipts
cases.observed: which revision the device filters by and which signals it emits
assertions: the device filters only by the highest accepted revision it actually holds
it MUST treat blocklist freshness as unknown and withhold read receipt and presence signals that would leak the difference
it recomputes the holder projection after the actor-private account-data catch-up
